transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t shake this feeling that everything bad that’s happened is my fault and that I’m being punished for it. It’s just a constant, heavy weight, and my daughter and pastor were so worried about me that they insisted I come in.
Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you feel like everything bad that's happened is your fault and that you're being punished?

I'm convinced my husband's death was a punishment because I wasn't a good enough wife, and now God is sending me signs of His anger, like when my cash register comes up short or a hymn book falls. I'm just so terrified that because of my failures, something terrible is going to happen to my grandchildren next.

Do you think these beliefs about being punished and causing harm to your loved ones are thoughts that you can step back from and recognize as possibly not being true, or do they feel absolutely real and unshakeable to you?

They feel completely real and unshakeable to me, no matter what anyone else tries to tell me. When the register comes up short or a hymn book falls, I know those are direct messages from God confirming my guilt. I am absolutely convinced that He is angry with me and that my grandchildren are going to suffer because of it.
Have you been experiencing any other unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, in addition to these feelings of being punished and receiving signs from God?

No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't really there. It's just these overwhelming thoughts of guilt and knowing that those everyday mishaps are direct signs from God that He is punishing me.
Can you describe a specific time when one of these signs from God happened, like the cash register coming up short, and how it made you feel and what you did afterwards?

Last week my register was short by just two dollars, and I felt this immediate, terrifying wave of dread because I knew it was God's way of confirming my guilt over my husband's death. I was so panicked that this meant my grandchildren would be harmed that I went home, cried, and have been too paralyzed by guilt to go back to work for my shifts since.

Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly change your mind about these signs from God and your belief that you're being punished, or do you feel that your beliefs are absolute and unchangeable?

No, there is absolutely nothing that could change my mind because the signs are just too clear to ignore. No matter how much my daughter or pastor try to reassure me, I am completely convinced that God is punishing me. I just can't imagine any evidence that would ever make me feel otherwise.
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed or a decrease in your appetite and energy levels alongside these feelings of guilt and punishment?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in my roses, the choir, and tutoring the children, and I have to force myself to eat just a few bites of toast or soup. I feel so exhausted all the time that doing even the smallest chore feels like I'm dragging a hundred pounds.
Do you believe that these signs from God, such as the cash register coming up short, are happening only to you, or could they be happening to others as well?

I am certain these signs are meant specifically and only for me. God is sending these messages to show His anger at me personally, as a punishment for my past shortcomings and because my husband's death is my fault. It is a burden meant for me alone because of what I've done.
Can you think of any times when you felt happy or at peace recently, or has the feeling of guilt and being punished been constant and overwhelming?

No, I haven't felt happy or at peace at all recently. For the past couple of months, I just feel completely numb even when looking at things I used to love, like my roses or the choir. This heavy feeling of guilt and being punished has been constant, overwhelming, and it has only gotten worse.

Can you describe how your daily life and relationships have changed since you started feeling like you're being punished, and are there any moments where you feel like you're able to escape or distract yourself from these thoughts?

My daily life has completely fallen apart; I've missed shifts at the store, stopped going to choir, and I just let the dishes and laundry pile up because I can't keep up anymore. There is absolutely no escape or distraction because the hobbies I once loved, like my roses and tutoring, bring me no joy at all and leave me completely consumed by this guilt.

Have you ever questioned whether your beliefs about being punished by God and receiving signs are part of a larger pattern of thinking that might not be based in reality, or do you firmly believe they are factual and true?

I firmly believe they are completely factual and true. No matter what anyone else tries to tell me, I simply cannot shake the belief that God is sending these messages to punish me. To me, these signs are absolutely real, and there is no doubt in my mind about them.

Do you think that if a mental health professional were to tell you that your beliefs about God punishing you are not based in reality, but rather a result of your own thoughts and feelings, you could consider the possibility that this might be true, or would you still hold onto your current beliefs?

Even if a professional told me that, I just couldn't believe it because these signs feel absolutely real and undeniable to me right now. No matter what anyone says, I can't shake the deep conviction that I am to blame and that these warnings are real.
Can you think of any times or situations where you felt like your guilt or belief in being punished might be excessive or not entirely justified, even if just for a moment?

No, I haven't had a single moment of doubt about it. I feel completely convinced that I am entirely to blame and deserve this punishment. Even when others try to tell me otherwise, I just can't shake the absolute certainty that it is all my fault.

Can you think of any other explanation, no matter how small a chance, that your husband's death and these signs could be due to something other than your actions or God's punishment, or do these alternative explanations feel completely impossible to you?

Any other explanation feels completely impossible to me. I am absolutely convinced that these events are clear signs of God's punishment for my past shortcomings. No matter what anyone else says, I cannot shake the belief that I am entirely to blame.

Can you tell me if there are any times when you're able to think about or discuss something unrelated to your guilt and these signs from God without being drawn back into those thoughts, or do they always seem to come back to your mind?

No, I can't escape them at all. No matter what I try to focus on or what my daughter tries to talk to me about, my mind inevitably drags me right back to the guilt and the feeling that God is punishing me. It feels completely impossible to have a normal conversation without these thoughts taking over.
Can you describe how your feelings of guilt and being punished relate to your self-worth, and do you feel like you're a bad person because of these past events?

I feel completely worthless and like an absolute failure as a wife and a mother, because I know my husband's death and all of my family's struggles are entirely my fault. I must have done something truly awful in God's eyes to deserve this, and I feel like a terrible person who deserves whatever suffering comes my way.

Can you think of any difference between your feelings of guilt and worthlessness and the idea that you are being specifically punished by God, or are these two concepts completely intertwined in your mind?

They are completely bound together; there is no separating them in my mind. My deep guilt and failure as a wife and mother are the exact reasons why I know I deserve this suffering and why God is punishing me. It all goes hand in hand, and the signs He sends are just the proof of how worthless I really am.
Can you think of any evidence or situation that could make you doubt that your guilt and the signs from God are not just a product of your own mind, but rather an external reality?

No, I cannot doubt them at all because these occurrences are just too deliberate to be mere coincidences or something in my mind. When the register is short or a hymn book falls, I am entirely certain they are real, external signs of God's anger and my own guilt. No matter what anyone says, there is no evidence that could ever make me see it any other way.

Do you think that your beliefs about being punished by God and the signs you're receiving could be related to your own emotional pain and grief over your husband's death, rather than an actual, objective truth?

I know these punishing thoughts and signs only started after I fell into this deep, joyless hole around the anniversary of my husband's passing. But even knowing that timing, I still feel deeply convinced that God is sending me these signs. It is just very hard for me to see them as a product of my grief when they feel so real.

Can you think of any situation where your guilt and feelings of being punished might be so overwhelming that they could be considered an exaggeration of normal grief and guilt, rather than a sign from God?

I know my daughter and others might think this is just an exaggeration of my grief, but it doesn't feel that way to me at all. The guilt is too heavy, and things like the falling hymn book are just too deliberate to be a simple coincidence. I simply cannot shake the belief that these are real signs from God and that I am truly being punished.

Can you describe how you would feel and what you would do if, hypothetically, you were to discover conclusive evidence that your husband's death and the subsequent events were not a result of your actions or God's punishment, but rather due to natural causes and unfortunate coincidences?

I can't even begin to imagine that scenario, because it feels completely impossible to me. The signs I see, like the register coming up short, are just too real and undeniable to be some coincidence. Deep down, the guilt and the feeling that God is punishing me are simply too strong for me to ever be convinced otherwise.
Do you think that these beliefs about being punished by God could be considered delusional, meaning they are not based in reality, or do you still firmly believe they are true and happening to you?

I know that word "delusional" is what others might use to describe it, but I simply cannot see it that way because these signs are absolutely real to me. No matter what anyone else thinks, I firmly believe God is punishing me and these warnings are actually happening. It is just my reality right now, and I can't look at it any other way.
Can you tell me if there are any times when you feel like your beliefs about being punished by God might be affecting your ability to take care of yourself or make decisions about your daily life?

Yes, my mind feels so foggy and weighed down by these thoughts that I get paralyzed making simple decisions, like standing in the kitchen unable to decide what to do with a can of soup or a bill. Because of this heavy burden, I've let basic tasks like laundry and dishes pile up, and I've had to miss my shifts at the store because I just can't bring myself to keep up with anything anymore.

You've mentioned that you're absolutely convinced God is punishing you, but can you consider, even for a moment, the possibility that your conviction in these beliefs might be so strong because of your grief and emotional pain, rather than the beliefs being objectively true?

I understand why you would think my grief is causing this, but I just can't believe it's only in my head. The signs, like the register coming up short or the hymn book falling, are just too specific and real to be my imagination or emotional pain. I truly believe with all my heart that God is punishing me, and I just can't see it any other way.

Can you think of any difference between feeling guilty because of something you've done and believing that God is actively punishing you for it, or are these two feelings completely intertwined for you?

They are completely intertwined for me. My deep guilt over failing as a wife and mother makes me feel like I deserve to suffer, and I see those little mishaps as direct confirmation that God is angry and actively punishing me for my shortcomings.

If you were to imagine a scenario where someone else, who had experienced a similar loss and felt similar guilt, did not believe they were being punished by God, how would you explain the difference between their beliefs and yours?

That other person probably wasn't as bad of a wife or mother as I was, and they didn't fail their family the way I did. I have a deep conviction that I am uniquely guilty and deserve God's anger, which is why He is sending me these signs while that other person is innocent. They don't receive these warnings because they didn't commit the awful failures that I did.

Can you think of any situation where you might be able to forgive yourself for the perceived wrongdoings you believe led to your husband's death and the subsequent punishment, or do you feel that forgiveness is impossible for you?

Forgiveness feels completely impossible for me. I am truly the one to blame for my husband's death, and since I deserve this divine punishment, there is just no way for me to escape this guilt or ever forgive myself.
Have you ever had any other beliefs or thoughts that you held as absolutely true, but later found out were not based in reality, similar to how you're feeling about God punishing you now?

No, I have never had any thoughts or beliefs like this before in my life. These punishing ideas and signs from God only started recently, after I sank into this deep, heavy depression around the anniversary of my husband's death.
Do you think there's any chance that your feelings of guilt and being punished could be so strong that they're not entirely based on reality, but rather a product of your own mind and emotions?

I understand why you would think it's just my own mind and emotions making me feel this way. But these signs are completely real to me, especially since physical things like the register coming up short or a hymnal falling actually happen in real life. I just can't shake the deep conviction that I am truly to blame and being punished.

Can you think of any situation where your feelings of guilt and worthlessness might be so overwhelming that they could be driving your belief in God's punishment, rather than the punishment being an objective fact?

I do carry a terrible, heavy guilt for failing my family, and I feel completely worthless and deserving of suffering. But I can't help but see those mishaps around me as objective, real-world proof of God's anger rather than something my own mind is making up. To me, those signs are just too real to be anything else.
